workedExamples.why: With a noun after aimer / adorer / détester / préférer, use the definite article (le / la / l’ / les). With another verb, use the infinitive without an article.

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Food & drink.
workedExamples.answer: Je bois de l’eau. / Je mange des frites.
workedExamples.why: When eating or drinking, use du / de la / de l’ / des

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Negatives.
workedExamples.answer: Je ne bois pas de coca. / Il n’y a plus de pain.
workedExamples.why: After ne…pas / ne…plus, change to de / d’

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Places after aller.

workedExamples.why: Choose au / à la / à l’ / aux carefully

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Passé composé.
workedExamples.why: Use auxiliary + past participle

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Être verbs.
workedExamples.answer: Elle est allée. / Ils sont sortis.
workedExamples.why: Movement / state verbs often use être and may need agreement
